report.headline: Measured g = 9.805 ± 0.053 m/s², just 0.01% below the reference 9.80665 m/s².
report.law: θ(t) = θ0·e^(−γt)·cos(2πt/T + φ), with T ≈ 2π√(L/g) corrected for finite amplitude, so g = 4π²L/T_small²

data_quality: Full coverage: 600/600 frames, no gaps, t=0-9.98 s; fit window 0.717-9.983 s (557 points)
Scale check excellent: blue sheet long side 10.034 px/cm vs short side 10.048 px/cm, agree within 0.1%

No warnings from pendulum fit; angle rms 0.029°
report.explanation: A red ball on a 55 cm string swings back and forth like a clock pendulum. Its swing angle follows a cosine wave whose height slowly shrinks because of air resistance and friction. Timing about six and a half swings very precisely gives the period, and combining that period with the string length gives gravity. The result, 9.805 ± 0.053 m/s², matches the accepted value 9.807 m/s², with the hand-measured string length limiting the accuracy.
next_steps: Measure the string length to the bob centre more precisely than ±0.3 cm, e.g. with a caliper/tape under tension, to cut the main uncertainty
Use a smaller release angle (<5°) to reduce the finite-amplitude correction
Film for longer to average more periods and watch damping over more cycles

meta.notes: string 55.0 cm from the knot to the bob centre
